entities.summary:
The Battle of Bagradas was a pivotal land engagement in the First Punic War, fought between Carthage and Rome in 254 BCE.

This clash of forces, fought on the outskirts of Carthage in modern-day Tunisia, proved a decisive victory for the Carthaginians, marking a turning point in the war.

The consequences of this battle would ripple forward, influencing the course of the war and the trajectory of the ancient world.

The First Punic War, a conflict fought between Carthage and Rome from 264 to 241 BCE, was a defining moment in the struggle for dominance in the Mediterranean world, shaping the course of history for centuries to come.

In the words of the Roman historian Polybius, 'the victory at the Bagradas River was a turning point in the war, for it restored Carthage's confidence and encouraged the Carthaginians to launch a fresh campaign against Rome.'
